subject: Current Affairs
q: Under the nuclear non-proliferation regime, IAEA "safeguards" are:
o: Inspections and measures to verify that nuclear material is not diverted to weapons
Insurance for nuclear power plants against accidents
Security guarantees given to non-nuclear states
Limits on the number of nuclear reactors a state may build
explanation: Safeguards are the IAEA's verification system of accounting, inspections and monitoring to confirm that nuclear material remains in peaceful use.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The IMF and the World Bank were created at the Bretton Woods Conference held in 1944 in:
explanation: The UN Monetary and Financial Conference met at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, USA, in July 1944.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The International Monetary Fund is headquartered in:
explanation: Both Bretton Woods institutions, the IMF and the World Bank, are based in Washington, D.C.

subject: Current Affairs
q: IBRD, the original institution of the World Bank Group, stands for:
o: International Bank for Recovery and Debt
International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
Inter-governmental Board for Reconstruction and Development
explanation: The IBRD was created in 1944 to finance the reconstruction of post-war Europe and later lent for development worldwide.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which of the following is NOT part of the World Bank Group?
explanation: The World Bank Group comprises the IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA and ICSID; the BIS in Basel is a separate organisation of central banks.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which arm of the World Bank Group provides interest-free loans and grants to the poorest countries?
o: International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes
explanation: IDA, set up in 1960, gives concessional financing to the world's poorest countries.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Within the World Bank Group, lending to and investing in the private sector of developing countries is the role of:
explanation: The IFC is the World Bank Group institution focused exclusively on private-sector development.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) mainly:
o: Lends to governments for balance-of-payments support
Insures foreign investors against political and non-commercial risks
explanation: MIGA, created in 1988, offers political risk insurance and credit enhancement to encourage foreign direct investment in developing countries.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Disputes between foreign investors and host states are commonly arbitrated at which World Bank Group institution?
explanation: The International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes, established in 1966, provides facilities for conciliation and arbitration of investment disputes.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Special Drawing Right (SDR) is:
o: A World Bank loan for infrastructure
A WTO safeguard against import surges
A trade credit issued by the Asian Development Bank
An international reserve asset created by the IMF
explanation: The IMF created the SDR in 1969 to supplement members' official reserves; its value is based on a basket of major currencies.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which currency was added to the IMF's SDR basket in 2016?
explanation: The renminbi joined the US dollar, euro, Japanese yen and pound sterling in the SDR basket on 1 October 2016.

subject: Current Affairs
q: A member country's voting power in the IMF is determined mainly by its:
explanation: Each member's quota, broadly reflecting its relative position in the world economy, determines its subscription, borrowing access and votes.

subject: Current Affairs
q: IMF "Article IV consultations" refer to:
o: Regular reviews of a member's economic policies
Debt write-offs for the poorest countries
Negotiations to change a member's quota
explanation: Under Article IV of its Articles of Agreement, the IMF holds usually annual surveillance discussions with each member on its economic and financial policies.

subject: Current Affairs
q: By a long-standing convention, the President of the World Bank has always been a national of:
explanation: Under an informal post-war arrangement, the World Bank has been led by an American and the IMF by a European.

subject: Current Affairs
q: By informal convention, the Managing Director of the IMF has traditionally been:
explanation: Since 1946 every IMF Managing Director has been European, balancing the American leadership of the World Bank.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Bank for International Settlements, often called the "central bank of central banks", is located in:
explanation: The BIS, founded in 1930, is based in Basel, Switzerland, and fosters cooperation among central banks.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The World Trade Organization began functioning in:
explanation: The WTO came into being on 1 January 1995, replacing the GATT framework that had governed trade since 1948.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The headquarters of the World Trade Organization is in:
explanation: The WTO secretariat is based in Geneva, Switzerland.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The agreement establishing the World Trade Organization was signed in 1994 at:
explanation: The Marrakesh Agreement, signed in April 1994, concluded the Uruguay Round and established the WTO.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The WTO was the outcome of which round of multilateral trade negotiations?
explanation: The Uruguay Round (1986–1994) created the WTO and extended trade rules to services, intellectual property and agriculture.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Doha Development Round of WTO negotiations was launched in:
explanation: WTO ministers launched the Doha Round in November 2001 with a focus on the needs of developing countries; it has never been concluded.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The highest decision-making body of the WTO is the:
explanation: The Ministerial Conference, which usually meets every two years, can take decisions on all matters under WTO agreements.

subject: Current Affairs
q: GATT, the forerunner of the WTO, stands for:
o: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
Global Arrangement on Trade and Tariffs
General Accord on Tariffs and Transport
Group for Agreement on Trade and Taxes
explanation: GATT was signed in 1947 and regulated world trade provisionally until the WTO was set up in 1995.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Decisions in the WTO are normally taken by:
o: Weighted voting based on trade volume
A vote of the five largest economies
explanation: The WTO follows the GATT practice of decision-making by consensus, giving every member, large or small, an effective voice.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) is headquartered in:
explanation: The OECD, founded in 1961 as successor to the Marshall Plan's OEEC, is based in Paris.

subject: Current Affairs
q: OPEC was founded in 1960 at a conference held in:
explanation: Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela founded OPEC at the Baghdad Conference in September 1960.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The headquarters of OPEC is located in:
explanation: OPEC moved its secretariat from Geneva to Vienna in 1965.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which of the following was one of the five founding members of OPEC?
explanation: OPEC's founders were Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela; Libya, Algeria and Nigeria joined later.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is headquartered in:
explanation: The China-initiated AIIB, which began operations in 2016, has its headquarters in Beijing.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank began operations in:
explanation: The AIIB's Articles of Agreement entered into force in December 2015 and it opened for business in January 2016.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Asian Development Bank, founded in 1966, has its headquarters in:
explanation: The ADB, which lends to developing member countries across Asia and the Pacific, is based in Manila, Philippines.

subject: Current Affairs
q: By tradition, every President of the Asian Development Bank has been a national of:
explanation: Japan, a co-largest shareholder with the USA, has supplied every ADB President since the bank's founding in 1966.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The New Development Bank, set up by the BRICS countries, is headquartered in:
explanation: The BRICS leaders agreed at Fortaleza in 2014 to establish the NDB with its headquarters in Shanghai.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Islamic Development Bank is headquartered in:
explanation: The IsDB, created under the OIC framework to finance development in Muslim countries, is based in Jeddah.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) is headquartered in:
explanation: IRENA, founded in 2009, is based in Masdar City, Abu Dhabi.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The International Energy Agency was founded in 1974 in response to:
explanation: Industrialised countries set up the IEA within the OECD framework after the 1973 Arab oil embargo to coordinate responses to supply disruptions.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The headquarters of INTERPOL is in:
explanation: INTERPOL, the international criminal police organisation, has its General Secretariat in Lyon, France.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The International Criminal Court was established by the:
explanation: The Rome Statute was adopted in 1998 and entered into force in 2002, creating the ICC in The Hague.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Unlike the International Court of Justice, the International Criminal Court tries:
explanation: The ICC prosecutes individuals for genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and aggression, whereas the ICJ settles disputes between states.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which of the following crimes is NOT within the jurisdiction of the ICC under the Rome Statute?
explanation: The Rome Statute covers four core crimes: genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and aggression.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The International Committee of the Red Cross was founded in 1863 at the initiative of:
explanation: Henry Dunant, moved by the suffering he saw at the Battle of Solferino, inspired the founding of the ICRC in Geneva.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW), which implements the Chemical Weapons Convention, is based in:
explanation: The OPCW, awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2013, is headquartered in The Hague.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The World Economic Forum holds its well-known annual meeting in:
explanation: The WEF, a Swiss-based foundation, gathers political and business leaders each January in Davos.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Permanent Court of Arbitration, which handled the 2016 South China Sea case, was established in 1899 and is located in:
explanation: The PCA was set up by the 1899 Hague Convention and sits in the Peace Palace, which it shares with the ICJ.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Financial Action Task Force was established in 1989 by:
explanation: The G7 summit in Paris created the FATF in 1989 to combat money laundering; its mandate was extended to terrorist financing after 2001.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The secretariat of the Financial Action Task Force is located in:
explanation: The FATF secretariat is housed at the OECD headquarters in Paris.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The FATF "grey list" is officially called the list of:
o: High-risk jurisdictions subject to a call for action
explanation: Grey-listed jurisdictions are working with the FATF to address strategic deficiencies; the black list is the list of high-risk jurisdictions subject to a call for action.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The FATF's international standards against money laundering and terrorist financing are set out as:
explanation: The FATF Recommendations, now 40 in number, form the global standard that countries are assessed against.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Nuclear Suppliers Group was formed in the mid-1970s in reaction to the nuclear test conducted in 1974 by:
explanation: India's 1974 test, using material from a civilian programme, led supplier states to coordinate export controls on nuclear material and technology.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Commonwealth Secretariat is located in:
explanation: The Commonwealth Secretariat has been based at Marlborough House, London, since its creation in 1965.

subject: Current Affairs
q: CHOGM stands for:
o: Council of Heads of Governments of Member states
Conference of Heads of Government of Muslim states
explanation: CHOGM is the biennial summit of the leaders of Commonwealth countries.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The London Declaration of 1949, which allowed republics to remain members, created the modern:
explanation: The 1949 Declaration let India remain a member after becoming a republic, recognising the British monarch as Head of the Commonwealth.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The first summit of the Non-Aligned Movement was held in 1961 in:
explanation: Leaders of 25 countries met in Belgrade, Yugoslavia, in September 1961 for the first NAM summit.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Bandung Conference of 1955, a forerunner of the Non-Aligned Movement, was a gathering of:
explanation: Twenty-nine Asian and African countries met at Bandung, Indonesia, to promote cooperation and oppose colonialism.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which of the following leaders was a founding figure of the Non-Aligned Movement?
explanation: Tito of Yugoslavia, with Nehru, Nasser, Sukarno and Nkrumah, led the creation of NAM to keep newly independent states out of Cold War blocs.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Group of 77, the largest coalition of developing countries at the UN, was formed in:
explanation: The G-77 was established by 77 developing countries in June 1964 at the end of the first UNCTAD session in Geneva.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Under the SAARC Charter, decisions are taken on the basis of unanimity and:
o: Each member has a veto only on trade matters
Bilateral and contentious issues are excluded from deliberations
The chair has a casting vote
Security issues are decided by majority
explanation: Article X of the Charter requires unanimity and keeps bilateral and contentious issues off the agenda, which has limited the body's effectiveness.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The idea of a South Asian regional organisation that became SAARC was first proposed by:
o: J. R. Jayewardene of Sri Lanka
explanation: Bangladesh President Ziaur Rahman circulated the proposal for regional cooperation in South Asia in 1980.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which of the following is a member of BIMSTEC but not of SAARC?
explanation: BIMSTEC links five South Asian states (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka) with Myanmar and Thailand; Pakistan, Afghanistan and Maldives are not members.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) among Pakistan, Iran and Turkey was established in:
explanation: RCD was set up in July 1964 to promote economic cooperation among the three states; it was revived as ECO in 1985.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The basic charter of the Economic Cooperation Organization is the Treaty of:
explanation: The Treaty of Izmir, originally of 1977 and later amended, is ECO's founding legal instrument.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Economic Cooperation Organization?
explanation: ECO's ten members are Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan, Turkey, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation was founded in:
explanation: The SCO was established in Shanghai on 15 June 2001 by China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation grew out of a grouping formed in 1996 known as the:
explanation: The Shanghai Five (China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan) was created to build confidence along their borders.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Secretariat of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation is located in:
explanation: The SCO has two permanent bodies: the Secretariat in Beijing and the Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure in Tashkent.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Iran became a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation in:
explanation: Iran was admitted as a full member at the SCO summit hosted virtually by India in July 2023.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which European country became a full member of the SCO at the Astana summit in 2024?
explanation: Belarus was admitted as the SCO's tenth full member in July 2024.

subject: Current Affairs
q: CICA stands for:
o: Council for International Cooperation in Asia
Central Asian Integration and Cooperation Alliance
Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia
Commission on Investment and Commerce in Asia
explanation: CICA is a pan-Asian forum for enhancing cooperation towards peace, security and stability in Asia.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) was proposed in 1992 by:
explanation: President Nursultan Nazarbayev of Kazakhstan proposed CICA at the UN General Assembly in October 1992.

subject: Current Affairs
q: ASEAN was established in 1967 through a declaration signed in:
explanation: The Bangkok Declaration of 8 August 1967 created ASEAN.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The ASEAN Secretariat is located in:
explanation: The ASEAN Secretariat has been based in Jakarta, Indonesia, since 1976.

subject: Current Affairs
q: ASEAN stands for:
o: Alliance of South and East Asian Nations
Association of Southern and Eastern Asian Nations
explanation: ASEAN is the regional organisation of Southeast Asian states promoting economic, political and security cooperation.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which of the following was NOT one of the five founding members of ASEAN?
explanation: ASEAN's founders were Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand; Vietnam joined in 1995.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The ASEAN Regional Forum, a platform for dialogue on political and security issues in the Asia-Pacific, was launched in:
explanation: The ARF held its first meeting in Bangkok in 1994; Pakistan joined it in 2004.

subject: Current Affairs
q: APEC stands for:
explanation: APEC is a forum promoting free trade and economic cooperation around the Pacific Rim.

subject: Current Affairs
q: APEC was established in:
explanation: APEC began as an informal ministerial dialogue in Canberra in 1989.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The APEC Secretariat is based in:
explanation: APEC established its secretariat in Singapore in 1993.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad) brings together:
o: The USA, India, Japan and Australia
The USA, UK, France and Germany
Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand
explanation: The Quad is an informal strategic forum of four Indo-Pacific democracies, widely seen as a response to China's rise.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Under the AUKUS pact announced in 2021, which country is to acquire nuclear-powered submarines?
explanation: AUKUS is a trilateral security partnership of Australia, the UK and the USA whose first pillar helps Australia acquire nuclear-powered, conventionally armed submarines.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The "Five Eyes" is an intelligence-sharing alliance of the USA, UK, Canada, New Zealand and:
explanation: The Five Eyes arrangement grew out of Anglo-American wartime cooperation and links the intelligence agencies of five English-speaking countries.
